name: the shared prefix is not hidden
why: Without the hoist mark every entry still renders its full "» month: February", which is the repetition the grouped layout exists to remove.
grep: groups by topic, merges a one-section topic

name: a one-section topic is not merged
why: Without merging, a topic with one sub-section shows two header rows for one list, and its header never reads "Topic › Sub".

name: the auto-collapse threshold is ignored
why: A sub-section over the threshold must open collapsed. Returning false makes the setting a no-op.
grep: auto-collapses a sub-section above the threshold

name: a stored expand does not beat auto-collapse
why: The user decided that a section expanded on its own stays expanded. Honouring only a stored "collapsed" re-collapses it on every open.

edits.find: if (stored === true || stored === false) return stored;

name: a Ctrl+Click expand-all is remembered
why: If expand-all stores "expanded" for every section, auto-collapse never applies to them again.
grep: Ctrl\+Click on a sub-heading acts on that topic only

name: Ctrl+Click on a sub-heading reaches every section
why: On a nested sub-heading Ctrl+Click is scoped to its own topic. The pre-grouping scope (every section) collapses unrelated topics too.
grep: Ctrl\+Click on a sub-heading acts on that topic only

name: Ctrl+Click on a main header acts on its own group only
why: Ctrl+Click on a main header applies to every main header, a merged section included.
grep: a main header collapses its topic

name: the quick filter does not open a collapsed topic
why: A collapsed group must never hide a live search result; without the forcing its matches stay inside a hidden body.
grep: quick filter matches the hidden prefix

name: old stored expanded marks are kept
why: Before grouping, false only meant "not collapsed" and Ctrl+Click wrote it for every section. Kept, it would disable auto-collapse wherever it was ever written.

name: the kill switch is ignored
why: sa_uvd_grouped_sections off must give the flat layout back, for bisecting and for anyone who prefers it.
